name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of cortical lamination abnormalities without dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells
Focal epilepsy refractory to medical treatment with seizure onset localized to a cortical region
MRI showing focal cortical thickening or blurring of the gray-white matter junction without balloon cells
Exclusion of other cortical malformations or tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of cortical lamination abnormalities plus clinical presentation of focal epilepsy and supportive neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires surgical biopsy or resection specimen; MRI findings may be subtle or negative.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with preserved awareness
searchTerms: seizures starting in one area with awareness
focal seizures without loss of consciousness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal cortical dyslamination identified on histopathology
searchTerms: abnormal brain cortex layering seen under microscope

common.symptomName: MRI evidence of cortical thickening or blurring
searchTerms: brain scan shows thickened or blurred cortex
seizure activity between episodes on EEG

occasional.symptomName: Focal motor deficits corresponding to lesion location
searchTerms: muscle weakness in specific body part

rare.symptomName: Developmental delay in early onset cases

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, or cortical dyslamination
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; some cases may have somatic mutations in mTOR pathway genes
other: Histopathology revealing abnormal cortical lamination without dysmorphic neurons or balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of dysmorphic neurons and balloon cells on histopathology
Multiple cortical tubers and subependymal nodules on imaging
Systemic manifestations including skin lesions and renal angiomyolipomas
Genetic confirmation of TSC1 or TSC2 mutations

redFlags: Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits
Rapid progression of seizure frequency or severity
Failure to respond to multiple antiepileptic drugs
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification. Epilepsia. 2011 Jun;52(6):158-174.
International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia, 2011.
Orphanet: Isolated focal cortical dysplasia type I (ORPHA:268961).
